build_scanned_ms.description: When the build was last scanned (ms since the epoch).

category_rules.description:
The project's own terms for sorting items into categories; they win over the built-in
keywords ([`crate::asset_categories::CategoryRule`]).

last_style.description: The style the person last chose for this project's local AI rebuilds.

notes.description: What the last scan of each source left out or couldn't do, in words.

original_folder.description: The original's folder at that scan.

original_scanned_ms.description: When the original was last scanned.

thing_merges.description: Things merged into another (thing key → the key it went into).

thing_names.description: Things renamed by a person or an agent (thing key → name).

Category.description: What an asset is for in the game.

oneOf.description: The player and their gear and voice.
Weapons and tools.
Items and pickups.
Machines and props: vehicles, turrets, pods, crates.
HUD and menus: icons, buttons, fonts, menu and UI sounds, menu video.
Terrain, rocks, caves, sky, ambience.
Particles, emitters, trails, impacts.
Not sorted yet.
The rules (the project's terms, the built-in keywords, the kind); applied again on rescans.
An agent (project_inventory_categorize); kept on rescans.
The person; kept on rescans, and an agent's choice doesn't replace it.

CategoryRule.description:
A project's own term: items whose name, path or origin has it go to `category`. Wins over
the built-in keywords.

term.description: A word (`glyphid`) or words (`bugs small`), matched like the built-in keywords; any case.

bytes.description: Its size on disk (or inside the original, when it wasn't taken out).

category.description: What it is for in the game ([`crate::asset_categories`]).

category_by.description: Who chose the category: the rules, an agent or the person (who wins over an agent).

described_by.description: Who wrote the description: the AI backend's name, or "person".

description.description:
What it shows and what it's for in the game, in a sentence or two (asset_describe), used
when it's remade.

detail.description:
What it is in more words (an Unreal package's class, a sound bank's codec, what a generated
asset was made from).

id.description:
Stable: a hash of the source and the item's key (`path` for the build, `origin` for the
original), so it survives rescans.

marked_ms.description:
When the person last set its status or note (ms since the epoch); a rescan keeps a marked
item's status and note.

name.description: What it's called (the file's name, or the asset's name inside the original).

origin.description:
For the original: where it is in the original, relative to the original's folder
(`<archive>[:<file inside>]#<object id>`, or a loose file's path).

path.description:
The file, relative to the project folder (`/`-separated). None for an item of the original
that wasn't taken out (`problem` or `detail` says why).

problem.description: What went wrong reading or taking it out, when something did.

rebuild.description: The rebuild it was sent to (project_inventory_rebuild), while it waits to be replaced.

role.description:
What it is, technically: a model, a model part, a colour texture, a normal map, a mask,
animation data, a sound, a voice line… ([`crate::asset_things::Role`]).

role_by.description: Who chose the role: the rules, an agent or the person.

thing.description: The thing it belongs to (an enemy, a character with its outfits, a voice group).

thumb.description:
A picture of it at most 256 pixels on a side (a PNG under reference/thumbs/), relative to
the project folder.

RebuildMark.description:
An item's place in a rebuild: how it's to be remade, when it was asked for, and the rebuild's
list (`rebuild/<category>-<time>.json`, by its file name without `.json`).

output.description: The file made for it (relative to the project folder), once one was.

oneOf.description: A piece of a model (a body, a helmet, a backpack, a beard, a tool).
A colour (albedo, base colour) texture or sprite.
Channels saying where effects apply (metal, roughness, emission…).
Positions or bones baked into a texture (`Armature_*`), not a picture.
A mesh for an effect (an emitter, particles).
An icon or other interface art.
A file of the build (app/).
Taken out of the original (Deep mode only), into reference/assets/.

Status.description: Where an item stands, for the person.

oneOf.description: The original's own asset.
Made by an asset generator (listed in assets.json).
From a library or pack (a marketplace or starter pack, an engine's own content).
A stand-in the builder made or took; the starting status of the build's files.
The person wants it replaced.
The person replaced it.

ThingRef.description: The thing a file belongs to.

key.description: Stable within the project: the category and the thing's stem (`enemies:glyphidgrunt`).

part.description: The part of the model this file is (`body`, `backpack`), for model parts and their maps.

sounds_only.description: A group of sounds or voice lines with no model or picture.

variant.description: An outfit or version (`Grid Runner`), when the thing has several.
